audit_findings.title: The earnings numerator and share denominator represent different economic claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 filed GAAP comparator: $352.9 million parent-attributable earnings versus $603.7 million fully converted earnings, a $250.8 million or 71.1% gap; exact OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The parent-attributable OE numerator is divided by 206.208 million Class A equivalents representing the whole partnership, depressing operating value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income attributable to Hess Midstream LP after deduction for noncontrolling interest of $352.9 million, or $2.87 basic earnings per Class A Share.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim-basis error, not merely a possibility. Its scale is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion, although the exact correction requires matching D&A, capital expenditures, working capital and conversion taxes to the selected ownership basis.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every OE component either for the parent claim divided by Class A shares or for the fully converted partnership claim, including incremental corporate taxes, divided by all Class A equivalents; rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: The seven-year trend is driven partly by changing ownership, not business growth
audit_findings.magnitude: The $231.3 million anchor is affected; weighted-average Class A shares increased from 56.2 million in 2023 to 123.1 million in 2025, or 119.0%, while consolidated net income increased from $607.7 million to $684.6 million, or 12.7%; corrected anchor unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Changing ownership alters the portion of partnership earnings attributed to the parent, contaminating the historical OE series and the log-trend anchor used in every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: Income tax expense in 2025 was $113.8 million, up from $71.8 million in 2024, which was primarily driven by increased ownership of the Partnership by Hess Midstream LP following the equity offering and unit repurchase transactions in 2024 and 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The changing claim is demonstrated, but its net effect on the fitted anchor cannot be established without a consistent historical reconstruction. Because the $231.3 million anchor drives the entire DCF, the distortion is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Restate 2019-2025 OE on a constant fully converted after-tax partnership basis, or calculate matching-claim per-share OE for each year; refit the trend and rerun all valuation scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The terminal value extends beyond the firm contract horizon
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed terminal value contribution is approximately $1,313 million to $1,975 million, representing 47.7%-51.5% of operating PV
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF projects through 2035 and capitalizes a perpetuity after the principal agreements and MVC protection end in 2033, without a renewal, tariff-reset or termination adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon the expiration of the Secondary Term, if any, the agreements will automatically renew for the subsequent one-year periods unless terminated by either party no later than 180 days prior to the end of the applicable Secondary Term.
audit_findings.explanation: Contract expiration is demonstrated, although termination or adverse repricing is not. Because roughly half of operating value depends on post-2033 cash flows that become annually terminable, carrying the existing economics into perpetuity without a reset is reasonably capable of overstating value materially.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the DCF with explicit 2034 cases for termination, reduced tariffs, loss or reduction of MVC protection, and continued renewal; report probability-weighted and standalone downside values.

audit_findings.title: The growth cases may conflict with falling guaranteed volumes
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2028 MVCs are 23.3%-28.2% below 2025 throughput across the five disclosed services; moving from the 6% bull case to the 0% bear case changes computed value by $5.25 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Lower throughput reduces revenue and OE, undermining the 3% and 6% growth paths and potentially the terminal earnings base.
audit_findings.evidence: To the extent our plans include revenues for volumes above currently established MVC levels, such revenues could decline to the MVC levels as a result of market volatility.
audit_findings.explanation: The declining contractual floors and recent volume weakness are demonstrated, but convergence to those floors is not. The model's own $5.25-per-share bear-to-bull spread establishes that the unresolved volume path is capable of materially affecting value.
audit_findings.action: Build service-level revenue and OE forecasts using the 2026-2028 MVC schedule, actual excess volumes, shortfall-credit mechanics and Chevron drilling assumptions; include a case that converges to MVCs and rerun the DCF.

audit_findings.title: Uncapped sponsor charges can outrun capped tariff escalation
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed sponsor charges were $114.7 million in 2025; first-half 2026 charges were $45.0 million versus $60.2 million in first-half 2025; future excess is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Sponsor operating and administrative charges reduce OE and margins; growth above capped tariff escalation would lower forecast and terminal OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The costs and expenses for which we are required to reimburse our general partner and its affiliates are not subject to any caps or other limits.
audit_findings.explanation: The contracts permit uncapped charges, but historical charges are already reflected in OE and first-half 2026 charges declined year over year. Faster future escalation is therefore a forward-looking risk rather than a demonstrated current valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Track quarterly omnibus and secondment charges and allocation methods; rerun the valuation if normalized sponsor-charge growth exceeds tariff growth, and stress post-merger cost inflation above 3%.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement cash obligations may be absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed ARO is $26.2 million; an undiscounted full deduction equals approximately $0.13 per share, 0.7%-1.0% of scenario equity value and about 0.6% of the $21.29 gap between market price and bull value
audit_findings.mechanism: If retirement spending is not captured in recurring capital needs, the unfunded obligation should reduce the equity bridge or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the asset retirement obligation balance included in Other noncurrent liabilities was $ 21.1 million and the current portion included in Accrued liabilities was $ 5.1 million (2024: $ 14.4 million and $ 5.0 million, respectively).
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is genuine, but even deducting the entire recorded balance immediately would reduce value by only about $0.13 per share and would not alter the conclusion at a $39.91 market price versus an $18.62 bull value.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether expected retirement expenditures are included in recurring capital expenditures; if not, deduct the unfunded ARO once in the bridge and avoid double counting.
